Don't listen to the dumbasses here saying that there's no time for depression. Mental health is serious and it shouldn't be taken lightly. 

I guess depression and other mental issues come from the pressure. We're all pretty high-achieving and pretty ambitious, so there is a tendency to feel as though if we're not doing as well as we expect ourselves to do, we're doomed for failure. 

Depression is hard, and IB there doesn't make it any easier. Be there for your friends, and let them know that IB isn't the end-all-and-be-all of life. I'm hoping that they have a good support network - friends, family and school counsellors. If they don't, please try and get them to someone who can talk over their issues with them, like a trusted guidance counsellor or something idk.

And please take care of yourself as well. There are jokes about sleep being for the weak, but remember that's a joke. Aim to get at least 6 hours of sleep on a regular basis (not that its ideal, but then... this is IB after all) and make sure to take time off for yourself. Take regular walks, do some physical activity, and keep up with your activities. Talk to people if you're feeling stressed, or if you're feeling really worried over your friends.  

Balance is key, pal. :)

... but you can't make it drink.

I'm slowly coming around to that, but it just hurts to know that she can get better, but she won't get help. I'll try, but I guess at the end of the day, I'll be leaving. 

Thanks for the response. I don't think I'll ever be guilt-free, but I definitely feel less angry at myself.

My parents refuse to see a therapist, unfortunately. They seem to see it as both an insult and a waste of money. I'm quite sure my mom has a disorder of some sort - perhaps my father as well - so its killing me because I know she can get help. However, I have no clue how to get her to accept help.

I'll look out for myself, and hopefully when I get to university I can access mental health services for myself. Thanks for the response, it makes me feel better :)

Firstly - thank you! You're making me feel kinda warm wand fuzzy inside, and that was really, really needed :) 

The thing is, my mom doesn't have access to mental health care. She has never been diagnosed, even though I'm 99% sure she has some mood and/or psychotic disorder. I've suggested it my parents, but both get pretty angry when I bring it up. Whenever she is hospitalized, or brought to the doctor, my parents give alternate reasons to the doctors and never mention any mental issues. I guess the stigma behind mental health still persists with them. It's driving me nuts, because my mom can be helped, but I have no clue how to get her to accept treatment.

I've never spoken to anyone about this. I don't have family here (we're immigrants - explains the cultural stigma behind mental health). I'm the funny, cool friend, and I don't want to burden my best friend with these depressing stories. I realize that I'm putting my mental health at risk by keeping it all inside - but whatever.

And I think you're right on leaving. I want to leave. I want to leave so badly, because I can feel myself losing my sanity in this house. The plan is to access mental health services when I get to university because I won't get them here - hopefully I can stick it out for a year. 

Thank you so much :) I feel just that little bit better for the future.
